reply:
That changes it: bcrypt silently truncates at 72 bytes -> you do need a limit.

Two passwords differing only after byte 72 hash identically. Security risk: an attacker who knows one password can use it as a second password.

Solutions:
- Cap input at 72 bytes and reject longer ones
- Pre-hash the password (SHA-256 the input first, then bcrypt the hash) so bcrypt gets a fixed-length digest

Pre-hashing is cleaner if your API already accepts long passphrases. Capping is simpler if you control the input contract.
